clue.text: Ministries on casual break

indicators.note: casual suggests something loose and haphazard, so the letters of 'Ministries on' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Government departments taking an informal pause from their work.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is an interval or pause in a performance, a synonym for a break.

clue.text: Examples of popular positions

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
stances are positions or postures

explanation.surface: Illustrations of postures that are widely favoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances are cases or illustrations of something, synonyms for examples.

clue.text: Ship neat rum for player

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of 'Ship neat' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Send undiluted rum to a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, after Thespis, so a player on the stage.

clue.text: Part of core curriculum to come up again

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A school topic in the basic syllabus keeps reappearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen or appear again, as a theme returns.

clue.text: Bury ready for French to take

parts.note: to inter is to bury
prêt is French for ready

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to accept a burial on behalf of a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something a certain way is to understand or construe it: to interpret it.

clue.text: High quiet stream

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A softly flowing brook up in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill sound is high-pitched and piercing, so high in tone.

clue.text: Ordinary charge to speak

parts.note: O is short for ordinary, as in O level
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: The standard fee for giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: O for ordinary comes from the old British O (Ordinary) level school exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, to speak pompously.

clue.text: Fits spring on messaging service

indicators.note: on means next to, so the spring is followed by the messaging service

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
SMS is the text messaging service

explanation.surface: Bouts of rage at the arrival of spring alerts on a phone service.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden convulsions or outbursts, synonyms for fits.

clue.text: Ways of heading off depression before the Sabbath

indicators.note: before puts the shortened depression ahead of the Sabbath letter
heading off says the first letter of the word for depression is removed

parts.note: a valley is a depression in the land
S is a dictionary abbreviation for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Methods of fending off low spirits before Sunday comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow lanes or passages, and ways can mean routes or paths.

clue.text: Old-fashioned secretaries not completely prepared

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, so secretaries are PAS

indicators.note: not completely tells us to drop the final letter of the word for prepared

parts.note: set means prepared, ready

explanation.surface: Dated office assistants who are not quite ready for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Passé, from French, describes something no longer fashionable: out of date.

clue.text: Supply with gold before beginning to laugh and cry

indicators.note: before places the preceding pieces ahead of the letter from laugh

parts.note: to cater is to supply food or what is needed
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of the word laugh

parts.note: first letter of laugh

explanation.surface: Someone provides gold and then moves from laughter to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to make a shrill howling cry, like a cat at night.

clue.text: Flee in small vehicle with rejected agent

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for agent is written backwards

parts.note: a rep (representative) is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A getaway in a tiny car with an agent who has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarper is British slang meaning to run away hastily, to escape.

clue.text: Right to trust missing book provides help

indicators.note: missing tells us the letter for book is absent from the word for trust

parts.note: to believe is to trust

explanation.surface: Faith restored without the scriptures still offers some assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to ease their distress or aid them, a synonym for help.

clue.text: Crooks wail about community service?

indicators.note: about here means scattered around, so the letters of 'Crooks wail' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Criminals complain loudly about the unpaid work handed out as a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Community service' looks like the court sentence crooks would wail about; the question mark flags that it is really the profession serving a community.
explanation.definitionFit: Social work is the professional support of people and families, a service to the community.

clue.text: Article in part of electrical system is decaying

indicators.note: in says the article is placed inside the wiring

parts.note: wiring is the cabling part of an electrical system
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A report that an item in the house's circuitry is rotting away.
explanation.definitionFit: Withering means shrivelling and fading, as a plant does when it is in decline.

clue.text: Regularly applauds bonus

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of applauds, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps clapping gets an extra reward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or extra benefit, much as a bonus is.

clue.text: I quit idly, wandering in fluid state

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so the letters of 'I quit idly' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who gave up lazily now drifts about in a state of flux.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquidity is the condition of being liquid, a state of flowing like water.

clue.text: Defeat provided by one caught showing great joy

parts.note: to beat is to defeat
if means provided that
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A batsman out caught off a fielder looks blissful despite losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatific describes a blissful, saintly expression of supreme happiness.

clue.text: Barely impartial

definitions.meaning: first meaning: only ..., by a narrow margin

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of one short word: an adverb of narrowness and an adjective of fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb for scarcely and as an adjective for a fair, unbiased judge.

clue.text: Vessel with wine is shaken

parts.note: a jar is a container or vessel
red is wine

explanation.surface: A bottle of red wine gets a good shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Jarred means jolted or rattled, so disturbed and shaken.

clue.text: Monumental queues forming behind National, endlessly

indicators.note: behind puts the rearranged queues after the shortened word for national
endlessly says the last letter of the word for national is dropped

parts.note: national means belonging to the state

indicators.note: forming suggests the letters of queues are shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Huge lines building up behind the National Theatre that never seem to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuesque means tall and imposing like a statue, so grand and monumental in appearance.

clue.text: Substitute Queen rested by entrance to zoo

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
sat means rested

indicators.note: entrance to points to the opening letter of zoo

parts.note: first letter of zoo

explanation.surface: The monarch takes a seat near the gates of the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an artificial imitation used in place of the real thing, a replacement.

clue.text: Leaders of gardeners' and zoologists' unions meet privately to seek a higher offer

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letter of each of the six following words

explanation.surface: Union bosses from horticulture and zoology hold secret talks to push for better pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To gazump is, in British property dealing, for a seller to raise the price after agreeing a sale, chasing a bigger bid.

clue.text: Servant goes after farm animal in frenzy

indicators.note: goes after places the servant word behind the farm animal

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep on a farm
a page is a young servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A servant chasing a sheep around the farmyard in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, uncontrolled behaviour, a wild frenzy.

clue.text: Little time for tea or coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Only a moment to decide on a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine variety of coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Apparently removes end from items

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: read as ..., it would mean taking the tails, or ends, off something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags the whimsical reading: the prefix de- means removing, and tails are ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Details are the individual points or particulars of something, the separate items.

clue.text: Blue revolutionary left lodge

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for blue is written backwards

parts.note: blue means risqué, lewd

explanation.surface: A depressed radical abandoned a masonic lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to live or stay somewhere, as to dwell is to reside.

clue.text: Ninety featuring in subtle story published only by us

indicators.note: featuring in says the numeral is placed inside the word for subtle

parts.note: elusive means hard to grasp, subtle
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A newspaper boasts of a subtle tale about a ninety-year-old that only it printed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive is a news story carried by a single paper, a scoop no rival has.

clue.text: A home featured in newspaper is unsteady

indicators.note: featured in says the letters go inside the newspaper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
in means at home

explanation.surface: A property in the paper's listings looks shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling faint means dizzy and weak, so unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: Carefree and pleased to leave fortune to unknown quantity

parts.note: happy means pleased
go means leave
luck means fortune
in algebra Y stands for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Someone content to leave their fortune to chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy-go-lucky person is cheerfully unconcerned about the future, easy-going and untroubled.
